actionable_lessons: Call attention to people's mistakes indirectly.
Indirect criticism protects dignity while still making the problem visible.
definitions: Principle: Call attention to people's mistakes indirectly.
examples: 2 How to Criticize - and Not Be Hated for It Charles Schwab was passing though one of his steel mills one day at noon when he came across some of his employees smoking.
Immediately above their heads was a sign that said “No Smoking.” Did Schwab point to the sign and say, “Can’t you read?” Oh, no not Schwab.
Simply changing one three-letter word can often spell the difference between failure and success in changing people without giving offense or arousing resentment.
For example, in trying to change a child’s careless attitude toward studies, we might say, “We’re really proud of you, Johnnie, for raising your grades this term.
key_points: Calling attention to one’s mistakes indirectly works wonders with sensitive people who may resent bitterly any direct criticism.
